info.title: Graphersal dev server HTTP API (EXPERIMENTAL)
info.summary: The HTTP API of `graphersal --server`: EXPERIMENTAL, may change in any release.
info.description:
**EXPERIMENTAL.** The HTTP API of the Graphersal development server (`graphersal --server`), the playground's engine boundary over HTTP. It may change in any release, minor or patch; pin the exact Graphersal version and read this file from the same version (the server answers it at `GET /openapi.json`, with its own version in `info.version`). The server binds the loopback interface only and has no authentication besides the optional MCP token: it is a local development tool, not a production server.

Conventions: answers are JSON; an error is `{"error": "..."}` with a 4xx status (422 when the engine refuses). Form-like operations (`*/define`, `*/create`, `element/*`) answer 200 with `{ok: false, errors: [{field, message, help?}]}` for refused input. A page sends `X-Graphersal-Client: <id>` with every request so the change feed can name who committed. Request bodies are JSON (`Content-Type: application/json`). The schemas below are deliberately loose (objects with the documented keys); the authoritative descriptions of every answer are the Graphersal book's pages linked from `externalDocs`.

externalDocs.description: The dev server in the Graphersal book

get.description: What the page needs to switch to this server: `server` (`graphersal-dev`), `version`, `saveable`, `source`, `presets` (the limits in force), `mcp` (`{endpoint, readOnly, client}` or null), `ai` (`{provider, model, readOnly, sendsDataTo, maxToolCallsPerTurn}` or null; never the key), `damageFound`, `embedders`, `readOnly` (`--read-only`, or a Store the process may not write: every write is refused). Answered without the session.

`{version, commitSeq, recent: [{version, by, commitSeq, detail?}], view, mcp, damageFound}`; `by` is the client of the commit (`X-Graphersal-Client` of a page, `mcp`, or `ai` with the conversation id in `detail`). Polled by the page to reload on changes it did not make.

post.description: Cancels the session's running query (it is rolled back): `{cancelled}`. Does not stop an AI Chat turn.

get.description: The served graph's info (name, counts, schema mode, catalog counts, store).

post.description: Runs a script (Gremlin in Rhai, `g.gql(..)` for GQL) as ONE unit (it commits when the answer is `ok`, and is rolled back otherwise). The answer is the playground's ExecuteResponse: `{ok, terminal, results | table | subgraph | text, execution: {error?, profile?}, mutated, changes, change_summary, ...}`; a failing script is reported in `execution.error` with status 200.

get.description: `{statistics, memory, process, limits: {presets, defaults}}`: the graph's data counts, its memory footprint (incl. `workload_bytes`), the memory of the process beside it (`process.memory`: RSS, live heap; models; the AI Chat history with `--ai`) and the limits every query runs under.
The graph's memory usage (`memoryUsage()`): structure, index and property bytes.

post.description: The memory report: one row per (element, label, property) with bytes, value types, size histogram, distinct strings, compression and index use; labels; the structure's totals. Read-only. `{ok: true, report}` or `{ok: false, error}`.

requestBody.description: A spec; `{}` for a full report.

get.description: The workload statistics of the served graph: `{level, queries, properties, locks, jobs}` (level `off` outside a store), each row per channel with the windows `last_hour`, `last_two_days`, `last_ninety_days`. With `history` every row carries `history: [{start, count, failed, items, total_micros, max_micros}]` of that tier (an unknown tier is a 422).

parameters.name: history
parameters.description: A tier of buckets to add: minutes, hours or days.

get.description: The schema views of the graph (stored or inferred, per label).
The stored schema (`null` without one).
A schema inferred from the data (nothing stored).

post.description: The schema views of the given schema with the graph's label counts, `source: "given"`; nothing stored.
Stores the schema, validated against the data (422 with the violations).
Applies a JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7396) to the stored schema.
Validates a schema against the data; changes nothing.
Validates the stored schema with a patch applied; changes nothing.
The differences between the stored schema and the given one.

get.description: The drawing as columns (ids, label indices, captions, edge endpoints as indices), no properties.

post.summary: Draw the graph with a filter
post.description: The same columns with the Graph panel's filter applied before the limits, plus `matchedNodes`/`matchedEdges`; `degrees: true` adds in/out degrees. An invalid filter is a 422.
`{query}`: the Rhai query selecting the vertices and edges the filter shows.

The vertices within `hops` (1-5) along `direction` of the centre `ids`, plus `keep`, and the edges between them, bounded by `maxNodes`/`maxEdges`; `seeds`, `missing`, `hiddenEdges`, `leftOut`. 422 for an unknown id or a depth above 5.
The first vertices of some primary labels or the first edges of one label pair, with `sample: {kind, shown, total, complete}`.

get.description: Vertex labels with counts (the 40 largest) and label pairs with edge counts (the 200 largest).

post.description: Starts the engine's force layout of a drawing and runs its first slice: `{job, state, iterations, totalIterations, progress, elapsedMs, vertexCount, cached}`, with `positions` once done or cancelled.
Runs the next slice (`budgetMs` default 100, at most 500).
Ends the job, keeping the positions reached so far.

get.description: One element with its properties (the inspector); `null` when it no longer exists.
The element in the typed form (`{type, value}` per property): `{kind, id, label, labels, source?, target?, properties, readOnly}`.

post.description: Writes the changed and removed top-level properties as ONE commit: `{ok: true, changed, element}` or `{ok: false, errors}` (always 200).
The labels the edit mode offers for a new vertex, or an edge between `from` and `to`.
Creates a vertex or an edge as ONE commit: `{ok: true, created, element, drawn}` or `{ok: false, errors}` (always 200).
Deletes a vertex with its edges, or an edge, as ONE commit: `{ok: true, deleted, edges}` or `{ok: false, errors}`.

get.description: Every DSL function with its signatures, aliases and doc (completion).
The values of the DSL's token classes (`Order` -> asc, desc, shuffle).
The saved queries with their params, status, writes and effects.
One saved query with its body, dialect and meta; `null` when there is none.

post.description: `{ok: true, query}` or `{ok: false, errors}` (always 200); `replaces` renames in the same commit.
`{dropped}`.
The moved entry.
The call run as a dry run and rolled back: `{ok: true, changes}` or `{ok: false, error}`.
`{text}`: the call `g.query("name", #{..})` with the arguments as Rhai literals.

get.description: The catalog file `{"definitions": [..]}` (every kind).

post.description: Stores a catalog file in one commit: `{loaded, graph}`.

parameters.name: replace
parameters.description: true: drop the definitions the file does not have.

get.description: The compression rules with their stats.

post.description: `{ok: true, rule}` or `{ok: false, errors}` (always 200).
What candidate rules would save on the current data; changes nothing. `{ok: true, estimate}` or `{ok: false, errors}`.
`{dropped}`.
The rule's entry after a new dictionary and re-encode (422 when there is none).

get.description: The property indexes with their stats.

post.description: `{ok: true, index}` or `{ok: false, errors}` (always 200).
`{dropped}`.

get.description: `{timeZone, store, jobs}`: the system jobs, then the jobs of users, each with schedule, enabled, nextAt, last run, run counts, `scheduled`/`reason`; a user job with action, args, path and effects.

post.description: Defines or replaces a job of a user: `{ok: true, job}` or `{ok: false, errors}` (always 200).
`{dropped}`.
Switches a job on or off: its entry.
A system job's schedule (`null`: its built-in one): its entry.
Runs a job now: its entry (`last` = this run).

get.description: `{tier, buckets}`: the job's runs per minute, hour or day.

post.description: The storage advisor's recommendations (create or drop an index, add or drop a compression rule), each with evidence, cost, memory effect, impact (ordered by it), confidence and its command; `dismissed` and `applied` outcomes. Read-only. `{ok: true, advice}` or `{ok: false, error}`.

schema.description: The advisor's thresholds; `{}`: the defaults, `everything: true`: every candidate.

post.description: Recomputes the advice for `spec`, finds `id` and runs its catalog command (one commit): `{ok: true, id, kind, result}` or `{ok: false, error}`.

spec.description: The advisor's thresholds; `{}`: the defaults, `everything: true`: every candidate.

post.description: Hides it for `days` (without: for good); kept in the store's workload sidecar. `{ok}`.
Lists a dismissed recommendation again. `{ok}`.

get.description: The graph as GraphSON (`.json`), GraphML or a packed snapshot (`gsnap`, binary).

post.description: Writes the graph back to its `--graph` file (and the schema to `--schema`): `{path, format, bytes, warnings, schemaPath?, warning?}`.

get.description: `{store: null}` without a store, else position, snapshots, marks, WAL, creation parameters, damage, compaction.

post.description: Writes a checkpoint (422 with the diagnostic on failure; 409 without a store).
Names the current position.

get.description: A stored snapshot as `.gsnap` (no `commit`: the latest), with the store's embedding models (and their licences) unless `models=without`.

parameters.name: models
parameters.description: `with` (the default) carries the store's embedding models; `without` leaves them out.

post.description: Serves the state at `target` read-only: `{view, graph}`.
Closes the view.
Copies the state at `target` into a new store `dir`: `{fork}` (409: the directory exists).
Rolls the store back to `target` (the undone commits go to the attic unless `delete`).

get.description: One page of the commits of an attic entry with totals.

post.description: Replays an attic entry onto the live graph.
Copies an attic entry into a new store `dir`.
Deletes an attic entry.
Reads and checks every file: `{verify: {ok, problems, notes, ...}}`.
A verified backup into `dir` (default `<store>-backup`; an existing backup takes an increment).

get.description: `{compaction: {recommended, reason, reclaimableBytes, ...}}`.

post.description: Prunes and compacts the store; 409 with `marksUnreachable` when a prune would lose marks and `dropMarks` is not true.
With `--ai` (EXPERIMENTAL): a new conversation `{id}` owned by the page's `X-Graphersal-Client` (required). Without `--ai` every `/api/ai/*` is 404.
Starts a turn on the server: `{turn}` (409 while one runs; 403 for another client's conversation).

get.description: `{events, running, last}`: the events after `after` (user, assistant, tool_call, tool_result, error, done).

post.description: `{stopped}`: ends this conversation's turn only.

delete.description: Drops the conversation (history, pending call, running query).

post.description: With `--mcp`: the Model Context Protocol endpoint (Streamable HTTP, JSON answers, JSON-RPC 2.0 messages: initialize, tools/list, tools/call, resources/*). Its tools are described by `tools/list`, not here.

get.description: `{"status": "ok"}` while the process answers HTTP, also while the graph loads, a query runs or the server stops. Takes no lock and never waits for the session; exempt from the Host/Origin checks (it reveals nothing). `HEAD` answers the same without a body. For Kubernetes `livenessProbe` and Docker `HEALTHCHECK` (`graphersal health`).

200 `{"status": "ready"}` when the graph is loaded and the server serves queries; 503 `{"status": "loading"}` while the graph or Store loads (every other endpoint answers 503 then), 503 `{"status": "stopping"}` after SIGINT/SIGTERM. Takes no lock and never waits for the session; exempt from the Host/Origin checks. `HEAD` answers the same without a body. For Kubernetes `readinessProbe` (`graphersal health --ready`).
The OpenAPI description of this API (also at `/api/openapi.json`), with this server's version.
The same as `/openapi.json`.

E400.description: A malformed request (missing body field, not JSON).

E401.description: A missing or wrong MCP token.

E404.description: Unknown endpoint, id or a disabled feature.

E409.description: Not possible in the server's state (no store, a read-only view, a conflict).

E422.description: Refused by the engine (the diagnostic in `error`).
